original_question: In Euclidean 3-space E^3, are the only finite type surfaces minimal surfaces together with open portions of spheres and circular cylinders?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Conjecture 1.A: "The only surfaces of finite type in E^3 are minimal surfaces, and open portions of spheres and circular cylinders." ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact ambient space E^3, the correct object class (finite type surfaces), and exactly the three candidate classes named by the paper: minimal surfaces, open portions of spheres, and open portions of circular cylinders. It is therefore very close to the paper's official formulation. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))
missing_details: The paper's notion of a surface of finite type is not just a subset of E^3; it starts with a connected Riemannian surface M and an isometric immersion x:M→E^3. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))

To be self-contained, you should define "finite type": the position vector x must admit a finite spectral decomposition x=c+x1+⋯+xk with c a constant vector, each xi a nonconstant E^3-valued map, and Δxi=λixi for the Laplace operator Δ of the induced metric. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))

The conjecture is about all finite type surfaces in E^3, not only compact ones; the separate compact-only statement in the same section is Conjecture 1, whereas your draft is targeting Conjecture 1.A. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))

The paper phrases the nonminimal examples as "open portions" of spheres and circular cylinders, so that local pieces are included and the statement is not restricted to complete or closed surfaces. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))

If you want the question to be maximally paper-faithful, say "ordinary" spheres/circular cylinders or specify round 2-spheres and circular cylinders in real Euclidean 3-space. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))
refined_question: Let x:M→E^3 be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian surface into real Euclidean 3-space, and call M a finite type surface if its position vector field has a finite spectral decomposition x=c+x1+⋯+xk with c constant, each xi nonconstant, and Δxi=λixi for the Laplace operator Δ of the induced metric. Must every such finite type surface be either a minimal surface in E^3, or an open portion of an ordinary round 2-sphere, or an open portion of a circular cylinder? ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))
justification: The draft is not aiming at the broader Problem 1, which asks to classify all finite type hypersurfaces in E^{n+1} and, in particular, all finite type surfaces in E^3. Instead, it matches the narrower surface-specific conjecture stated immediately afterward as Conjecture 1.A in Section 3. Section 2.1 supplies the hidden formalism behind the phrase "finite type," while nearby discussion in Section 7 explains that circular cylinders are the only null 2-type surfaces in E^3, which helps explain why cylinders appear among the conjectured exceptions. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))

citations.label: Discussion after equation (7.1): circular cylinders are the only null 2-type surfaces in Euclidean 3-space
